prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape aspect ratio about 3:2, crisp vanilla Minecraft voxel style, plain light background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side: LEFT straight-on front elevation, strictly orthographic; RIGHT three-quarter front view at the same scale. Both show exactly the same build. Skilled human builder quality: substantial real massing, projecting bays and trim, recessed framed openings, verges, eaves and ridges, stairs/slabs/fences/walls/trapdoors/lantern details. Keep block grid and identifiable vanilla textures; no arbitrary smooth miniature architecture.

Site: Victorian townhouse terrace of three attached houses on a city street seen from the pavement. Total building 25 blocks wide (three 9-wide houses with shared party walls), 13 deep, about 26 high, on a 31 x 35 lot including street and back gardens. End houses are red brick, three storeys over grey stone-brick plinths plus small black-slate mansard attics. Each end house has a two-storey canted bay of cream sandstone on its INNER side, with large glass panes; a three-step stone stoop with black railing on its OUTER side leads to a painted front door, teal left and crimson right. Glass transoms and white quartz door hoods on brackets. Cream sandstone string course along whole row above ground floor, paired cream quoins on outer corners, cream sill and lintel at every window, flower boxes beneath top-floor windows. End houses have stone dentil cornices, small mansard roofs with real edges, one gabled dormer each and iron crests.
Centre house one storey taller, four storeys, smooth cream stucco. Dark oak front door behind white quartz portico with two columns; flat portico roof forms first-floor balcony with iron railing and French door access. Row of three tall windows on each floor, with the balcony French door integrated in the first-floor row. Quartz bracketed cornice, flat parapet with iron rail at top. Centre side walls visible above neighbours' mansards. Cream stone pilaster strips mark shared party walls. Exactly two tall brick chimney stacks on party walls through roofs, dark bands and smoking caps.
Foreground: black iron area railings, grey flagstone pavement and kerb, exactly two lamp posts and three young street trees, and an andesite road. Behind: three walled back gardens with paths and gates; reveal as much as the three-quarter view permits without changing the required front camera. No extra inset views.

Use this palette, exact vanilla block ids:
brick: bricks, brick_stairs, brick_slab, brick_wall.
sandstone: smooth_sandstone, smooth_sandstone_slab, smooth_sandstone_stairs.
cut_sandstone: cut_sandstone, cut_sandstone_slab.
quartz: smooth_quartz, quartz_pillar, quartz_stairs, quartz_slab.
stone_brick: stone_bricks, stone_brick_stairs, stone_brick_slab.
roof: deepslate_tiles, cobbled_deepslate, polished_deepslate, cracked_deepslate_tiles, polished_blackstone_bricks, smooth_stone.
chimney: bricks, deepslate_bricks, stone_brick_slab.
glass: glass_pane.
door: warped_door, dark_oak_door, crimson_door, spruce_door.
railing: iron_bars, polished_blackstone_wall.
street: andesite, gravel, smooth_stone, polished_andesite.
ground: grass_block, coarse_dirt, podzol, rooted_dirt, dirt_path.
floor: spruce_planks, dark_oak_planks.
Functional/decor blocks: campfire (chimney smoke), spruce_stairs, spruce_fence, ladder, spruce_trapdoor (flower boxes), spruce_fence_gate, lantern, iron_chain, flower_pot, potted_poppy, potted_cornflower, poppy, allium, azalea, oak_log, oak_leaves, black_stained_glass_pane.
Use actual vanilla shapes as needed. Add compact legible material labels naming representative blocks by exact ids, without covering the architecture. Keep all building and lot edges inside the sheet.
changes: Saved the unmodified generated image as concept.png in the current directory.

Block identities are visual interpretations and build equivalents; the image cannot establish every exact block state or distinguish all similar textures. The roles retain every planned block, including blocks not visibly confirmed.
Only two street trees are visible in each view, rather than three.
Flower boxes appear beneath windows on multiple floors, including the centre house, rather than only beneath the end houses' top-floor windows.
Extra shrubs, flower beds and potted balcony greenery fill the front areas and rear gardens.
The centre balcony opening reads as a glazed window; a functional French door is not clearly depicted.
Stoops appear to have more than three risers, particularly at the centre entrance.
The centre portico has additional wall-side supports beyond its two prominent front columns.
End-house dentil cornices look cream sandstone rather than grey stone.
The centre stucco and some trim have mottled sandstone-like textures rather than uniformly smooth surfaces.
Roof slopes, cornices, chimney caps, kerbs and garden details require additional stair, slab and wall variants listed in the roles.
White flowers are interpreted as oxeye_daisy, purple flowering shrubs as flowering_azalea, and blue flowers as cornflower; these add blocks beyond the supplied palette.
Decorative ironwork includes finials, fine balusters and curved-looking details that vanilla iron_bars cannot reproduce exactly.
Window muntins and some brackets are finer than vanilla block geometry, so the picture is not an exact block-placement blueprint.
The front elevation has slight top-surface visibility rather than being strictly orthographic; the three-quarter view is elevated enough to reveal all three rear gardens.
The two views are not demonstrably at the same block scale and differ in some planting and small details.
Dimension labels repeat the requested sizes, but actual block counts are not verifiable. The width label incorrectly displays '25 BLOCKS WIDE (9 + 9 + 9)' without explaining shared party walls.
The right view places the centre upper storey prominently above and toward the rear of its balcony mass; its exact alignment with the front elevation is ambiguous.
No ladder or iron_chain is clearly visible; several planned ground, floor and alternative door blocks are concealed or unconfirmed.
